title: unwith
summary: Removes with blocks, proving every name binds to what it bound before
intro: Read this when you want a with statement gone without a name silently changing meaning. --plan names, for every with in a file or a project, whether it can be removed and exactly why not; --apply rewrites through the compile gate, then re-indexes a copy of the DB and rolls back if any reference binds elsewhere.

surfaces.usage:
drag-lint unwith --db [--in [--line ]] (--plan | --apply --project ) [--platform

] [--rsvars ] [--build-timeout ] [--library-db |none] [--no-backup] [--build-config ] [--no-preprocess] [--json|--format json] - remove with blocks, proved binding by binding
help:
drag-lint unwith --db [--in [--line ]] (--plan | --apply --project ) [--platform

] [--rsvars ] [--build-timeout ] [--library-db |none] [--no-backup] [--build-config ] [--no-preprocess] [--json|--format json] - remove with blocks, proved binding by binding

drag-lint lint --fix --fix-rule with-statement --db [--in [--fix-line ]] [--apply --project ] [--platform

] [--rsvars ] [--build-timeout ] [--library-db |none] [--no-backup] [--json] - the same as `unwith`: no --apply = --plan
